correctness.rationale: Normalized Weyl integration converts the exact Peter--Weyl kernel into a one-dimensional absolute integral. The displayed finite trigonometric identity is algebraically exact. Its remainder has absolute integral \(O(\log M)\), while the leading weighted \(|\cos|\) term equals \(4/\pi+O(M^{-1})\) by its absolutely convergent Fourier series. Therefore the endpoint norm is \(\frac{8}{\pi^2}M+O(\log M)\). Finite checker output is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim refines the classical \(SU(2)\) spherical-partial-sum order estimate to an exact normalized leading constant. The closest inspected sources cover the decomposition or only two-sided growth, and literature/database alias searches do not yield a statement implying the coefficient. One plausible inaccessible Bochner--Riesz source is retained as a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full Dreseler 1986 Bochner--Riesz article was not available for direct statement-level inspection; an equivalent unsmoothed \(SU(2)\) coefficient hidden there or in older rank-one literature cannot be excluded.
Equivalent formulas may use a different spectral parameter normalization; the claim is therefore stated for the explicit highest-weight cutoff \(S_L\).

value.rationale: The canonical cumulative highest-weight projection is a fundamental nonabelian Fourier truncation. An exact leading endpoint amplification constant materially sharpens the previously checked order-only Lebesgue-constant estimate, and it is not a routine consequence of a single-block norm because cumulative kernel cancellation is essential.
